Of 166 individual repeat-runs, baseline hit NE=0 in only 9 (5%) vs soft_anchor's 123 (74%) -- consistent with the original clip's finding that anchoring reduces run-to-run flicker variance, not just its mean.

FIDELITY (translation_fidelity_judge.py, 1 repeat per span/condition, 166 judge calls total): mean score baseline_replay=92.95, soft_anchor_replay=89.04 (-3.9 points). This drop is larger in absolute terms than the original clip's (-0.6, 99.3->98.7), and this clip's BASELINE fidelity itself is already notably lower (92.95 vs 99.3) -- plausibly because this clip's source is intrinsically harder to translate cleanly (disfluent spoken interview vs the original's more monologue-like structure), which may also amplify any anchoring-side hallucination risk. Manually inspected the single worst case (span 69, judge score 0): source 'our paper, we just like a like like a AIM to' (a genuinely fragmentary, cut-off utterance). baseline's from-scratch retranslation of the fuller context produced a generic, non-committal continuation ('目指しているのは、その' -- 'what we're aiming for is...'), while soft_anchor's advisory-anchored continuation invented a specific but unsupported acronym expansion ('AIMEを目標としているかのようで' -- 'as if aiming for AIME'), a hallucination not present in the ambiguous source. This is a new failure mode distinct from h-hard-prefix-lock-continuation's mid-clause-split issue: soft-anchoring's continuation instinct can fabricate content to make an ambiguous/cut-off fragment cohere with its own prior translation, rather than staying agnostically vague like a from-scratch retranslation does. It appeared to affect a minority of spans (16/83 scored <80 under soft_anchor vs 10/83 under baseline) concentrated in spans with visibly disfluent/fragmentary source text (see the top-5 worst-delta spans, e.g. span 7 'based on the we will give you oh,', span 29 'future to pro promoting to let the answer some questions.').

RECOMMEND: the anchor_continuation_translation flag still looks like a good default given the NE win generalizes and is large, but flag the hallucination-under-disfluency failure mode explicitly if/when promoting it out of experimental status -- a future hypothesis could test whether gating the anchor off (falling back to from-scratch retranslation) specifically for very short/fragmentary source deltas mitigates this without losing the NE win on cleaner speech. hypotheses.title: Gate the soft-anchor continuation prompt off for very short/fragmentary source deltas to avoid the hallucination-under-disfluency failure mode while keeping the cross-batch NE win
hypotheses.description: h-soft-anchor-generalization-guest-talk confirmed soft_anchor_replay's cross-batch NE reduction generalizes (83% relative reduction on 83 guest-talk spans, even larger than the original clip's 65%), but also found the fidelity cost is clip-dependent and concentrated in disfluent/fragmentary source: mean fidelity dropped -3.9 points on the guest-talk clip vs -0.6 on the cleaner original clip, and manual inspection of the worst case (span 69, delta_text 'our paper, we just like a like like a AIM to') showed the anchor's continuation instinct fabricating a specific but unsupported acronym expansion ('AIME') to make an ambiguous, cut-off fragment cohere with its own prior translation -- a hallucination the from-scratch baseline did not produce (it stayed vague instead). That result_summary explicitly proposed gating the anchor off for very short/fragmentary deltas as the next concrete follow-up. This hypothesis implements and tests the simplest such gate: a per-batch word-count threshold on delta_text (the NEW source fragment for that batch, not the cumulative text) -- below the threshold, fall back to baseline (prior_translation=None, from-scratch retranslation of the cumulative text); at or above it, use the existing soft-anchor path unchanged. Tests on both already-replayed source experiments (the original 15-span clip and the 83-span guest-talk clip) to check the gate preserves the NE win on the clip where it was clean (minimal regression expected, few/no deltas are short there) while reducing or eliminating the fidelity drop on the guest-talk clip's short-delta spans (where the failure mode was concentrated).
hypotheses.predicted_effect: For spans whose short/fragmentary batches get gated to baseline: expect those specific batches' fidelity to move back toward baseline's (higher than pure soft-anchor), at the cost of losing some of the NE reduction on exactly those batches (baseline rewrites more). Averaged across all spans, expect gated_soft_anchor to land between baseline_replay and soft_anchor_replay on both metrics -- NE noticeably lower than baseline (most batches are not short, so most of the win is retained) and mean fidelity closer to baseline than pure soft-anchor is, with the specific span-69-style hallucination (inventing content to cohere with an ambiguous cut-off fragment) reduced or gone on gated batches. A null result (gating barely changes either metric) would mean the threshold picked is wrong (too low to catch the failure cases, or too high and gating too much) or that delta_text word count is not actually a good proxy for 'fragmentary/ambiguous' -- worth checking against the specific short-delta spans flagged in the guest-talk result before concluding either way.
